channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Jucá registra candidatura a deputado federal após decisões judiciais
item.description: Former senator Romero Jucá (MDB-RR) registered his candidacy for federal deputy from Roraima following provisional decisions by the STF and STJ that suspended the effects of his conviction for passive corruption and money laundering, linked to R$150,000 received from Odebrecht in 2014. Minister Flávio Dino (STF) ordered the case be returned to the Supreme Court, as the alleged crimes occurred during his senatorial mandate, while Minister Messod Azulay Neto (STJ) ruled the conviction does not bar him from running while the case is under review. Jucá, a three-term senator and former minister in the Lula and Temer administrations, had his candidacy registered, but it remains subject to final approval by the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Caiado declara mais de R$ 52 milhões ao TSE
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, presidential candidate for PSD-GO, declared R$ 52.557.930,98 in assets to the TSE, highlighting livestock (R$ 10.4 million) and other real estate (R$ 36.2 million). His government plan, presented with running mate Gilberto Kassab, proposes ending presidential reelection and adopting a mixed-district system for legislative elections.

item.title: De R$ 33 mil a R$ 242 mi: veja patrimônio declarado por presidenciáveis
item.description: Presidential candidates in the 2026 Brazilian elections declared assets ranging from R$33,000 to R$242.28 million, according to TSE data. This wide disparity highlights significant financial differences among those running for the nation's highest office.

item.title: Arruda declara R$ 830 mil; vice de sua chapa registra R$ 26,2 milhões
item.description: José Roberto Arruda (PSD), candidate for Governor of the Federal District in 2026, declared R$ 830,2 thousand in assets, a modest increase since 2022, while his running mate, Luiz Pitiman (PSD), declared R$ 26.2 million, revealing a significant wealth disparity in the ticket. Arruda has a history of administrative misconduct convictions, including being ordered to repay R$ 595 million to public coffers linked to Operation Pandora's Box, and is seeking to enable his candidacy despite ineligibility, relying on proposed changes to the Clean Record Law under discussion at the STF.

item.title: Suspeito de ameaçar Flávio é alvo de busca e apreensão em Juiz de Fora
item.description: A resident of Juiz de Fora (MG) was targeted in a search and seizure operation after being investigated for allegedly threatening Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a 2026 presidential candidate. He was taken in for testimony. The investigation began following a social media post.

item.title: Programas de Lula e Flávio fazem promessas sem dizer como vão bancar gastos
item.description: The government programs of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) contain numerous promises but fail to explain how they will finance the expenditures, according to economists analyzed by Folha.

item.title: Governo Lula pressiona Alcolumbre por fim da 6x1 antes das eleições
item.description: The Lula government intensified efforts to approve before the October elections a constitutional amendment ending the 6×1 work schedule, following three meetings between the president and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The PEC, already passed by the Chamber of Deputies, had been stalled in the Senate but had its unblocking announced on Friday (Aug 14) after a meeting at the Alvorada Palace. Alcolumbre, who previously resisted political-electoral pressure, signaled a shift in stance amid rapprochement with the Planalto Palace.

item.title: Zema: “Contra o PT voto até num copo”
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) stated he would vote for any candidate facing the PT in a potential 2026 presidential runoff. He hopes to receive support from other right-wing candidates if he advances to the second round. His remarks emphasize his ideological opposition to the PT, even if it means backing less-than-ideal alternatives.

item.title: Tarcísio dará pontapé inicial na campanha eleitoral com mulheres em Osasco
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) will kick off his 2026 electoral campaign with a women's roundtable in Osasco, SP, this Friday (16). The event will bring together homemakers, entrepreneurs, and community leaders to discuss their expectations for the state government over the next four years. The initiative highlights a strategic focus on social and gender issues in his campaign approach.

item.title: Ex-presidente do PSB cobra esquerda por mais repressão ao crime organizado
item.description: Former PSB president Carlos Siqueira argues that the left must reassess its public security policies, advocating for firmer repression against organized crime while maintaining social policies that address its root causes. He emphasizes that precarious youth, mothers heads of household, and evangelicals — groups feeling abandoned by the state — seek security as a response to institutional neglect. Concern over violence already dominates the pre-electoral debate, even before the official campaign begins.

item.title: 'Lula se apequenou em processo', diz Flávio sobre tarifas de reciprocidade contra EUA
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) criticized President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), calling him irresponsible after the start of a process that could lead to the application of the Economic Reciprocity Law against the U.S. Flávio claimed Lula 'diminished himself' by adopting reciprocal tariff measures, which he views as harmful to Brazil's economy and inappropriate amid ongoing trade tensions with the United States.

item.title: Empate técnico marca início da disputa presidencial entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro, aponta Quaest
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are technically tied at 43% and 40% respectively in a potential runoff, with a two-point margin of error, according to Quaest poll. The tie reflects a return to pre-May revelation levels, when Lula had an eight-point lead over Bolsonaro’s son. In the first-round scenario, Lula leads with 38% to Flávio’s 31%, with the senator’s recovery driven by Southeast voters, evangelicals, and independents.

item.title: Quaest: os grupos em que a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro está mais apertada
item.description: The Quaest poll shows a technical tie between Lula (43%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (40%) in the 2026 runoff, with the difference within the margin of error. Lula leads among youth (16-34), Northeast, low income, Black voters, and Catholics, while Flávio wins among men, South, evangelicals, and high income. Independent voters (33% of the electorate) favor Flávio (35% vs 29%), and women lean toward Lula (44% vs 35%).

item.title: Amiga de Lulinha ainda luta para ter acesso a inquéritos no STF
item.description: Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of Lulinha (President Lula’s son) under investigation for influence peddling, still has not gained access to the STF inquiries, despite her messages with businessman ‘Careca do INSS’ and Lula’s son being central to the investigations. She is also linked to a R$249,000 payment to Lula’s former chief of staff, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), who claims it was a repaid loan. The case involves two STF rapporteurs — Flávio Dino and André Mendonça — due to the separate inquiries into Lulinha’s alleged scheme.

item.title: Proporção de editoriais críticos ao STF sobe em 4 jornais
item.description: The proportion of editorials critical of the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) increased in the first half of 2026 across four major newspapers, with Folha de S.Paulo showing the largest rise at 15.14 percentage points. The Ranking dos Políticos analyzed 1,833 editorials from 2023 to June 2026, finding that criticism focused on monocratic decisions, the Banco Master case, and perceived power concentration. Despite the rise in criticism, outlets like O Globo and Folha acknowledged the STF’s role in defending democracy and institutions.

item.title: Vice-campeã do BBB 17, Vivian Amorim sai candidata e expõe bens ao TSE
item.description: Vivian Amorim, runner-up of BBB 17 and member of the União Brasil party, is running for federal deputy from Amazonas, having declared a net worth of R$ 3.4 million to the TSE. She owns two residential properties (in São Paulo and Manaus), over R$ 768,000 in investment funds, R$ 100,000 in her individual company’s capital, and bank balances, in addition to earning R$ 150,000 during the reality show. The article highlights how she leveraged her BBB fame to build wealth and enter politics.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Candidatos à Presidência declaram patrimônios que variam de R$ 30 mil a R$ 242 milhões ao TSE
item.description: The asset declarations of presidential candidates to the TSE reveal extreme wealth disparity, ranging from R$ 33,000 (Samara Martins, UP) to R$ 242 million (Augusto Cury, Avante). Cury leads with assets driven by loans, corporate holdings, and stocks, followed by Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD). Declarations are mandatory for candidacy registration and publicly accessible via DivulgaCand.

item.title: Tarcísio dará pontapé inicial na campanha eleitoral com roda de conversa com mulheres em Osasco
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas launches his 2026 electoral campaign with a women's forum in Osasco, aiming to boost his support among female voters, as polls show 50% male support versus 34% female support. The event highlights proposals for 24-hour women's police stations and phase-specific health programs, while signaling an initial focus on the São Paulo metropolitan region, where his main rival Haddad outperformed him in 2022.

item.title: ‘Lula se apequenou em processo’, diz Flávio sobre tarifas de reciprocidade contra EUA
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) accused President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) of having 'diminished himself' in the process of applying the Economic Reciprocity Law in response to U.S. tariffs on Brazilian steel and aluminum. He claimed Lula acted irresponsibly by provoking the U.S. and is now focused only on re-election, not national interest. Flávio also denounced a alleged fraudulent affiliation with the Missão party, claiming he was a victim of an electoral crime.

item.title: Governo Lula ganha fôlego para o Orçamento, mas ajuste em 2027 segue inevitável, dizem economistas
item.description: The Lula administration has secured temporary room to finalize the 2026 Annual Budget Bill (PLOA) by the August 31 deadline, following recent revenue and expenditure adjustments. However, economists warn that structural fiscal adjustment remains inevitable in 2027 due to persistent spending pressures and primary deficit targets.

item.title: Renan Santos relata ameaça de morte e aciona Polícia Federal
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) reported receiving a death threat detailing a plan to shoot him on August 16, 2026, the date of his official campaign launch at Largo de São Francisco in São Paulo. The anonymous message, allegedly from a USP law student, claims he purchased an illegal firearm on the dark web and labels Santos a 'Nazi' and 'Brazil's top fascist leader' as justification. Despite the threat, Santos affirmed the event will proceed with heightened police presence and confirmed he has filed a report with the Federal Police.

item.title: Veja a identidade visual da campanha de Lula
item.description: The re-election campaign of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will use the slogan 'Brazil ready for more' as its visual identity, incorporating the colors of the Brazilian flag (PT red, green, yellow, and blue) to highlight Lula and his running mate, Geraldo Alckmin (PSB). The coalition includes PT, PC do B, PV, PDT, PSB, Psol, and Rede. The official launch will take place on August 16, 2026, in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), with an expected attendance of 20,000 people.

item.title: Cantor Frank Aguiar volta à política com patrimônio encolhido
item.description: Singer Frank Aguiar has registered his candidacy for federal deputy from São Paulo under the Podemos party, declaring a net worth of approximately R$ 2 million, primarily from a residential property. He aims to return to the Chamber of Deputies exactly 20 years after his first election in 2006 under the PTB party. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Fiesp critica tramitação “apressada” do fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Fiesp criticized the 'rushed' processing of the PEC ending the 6x1 work scale, stating the issue requires technical debate and should not be influenced by the electoral calendar. The proposal, already approved by the Chamber, was sent to the Senate's CCJ and may be voted after the October elections. The federation argues working hours should be negotiated sectorally, not imposed constitutionally.

item.title: Líder do PT na Câmara, Pedro Uczai recebe alta da UTI após sofrer AVC
item.description: The leader of the PT in the Chamber of Deputies, Pedro Uczai (SC), was discharged from the ICU on Saturday morning (15/8) after suffering a stroke during a leaders' meeting on Tuesday (11/8). He remains hospitalized but shows good clinical progress, is conscious, and has no cognitive or motor impairment, with expected discharge from hospitalization on Monday (17/8). Uczai received a visit from Chamber President Hugo Motta and a phone call from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

item.title: Como a Polícia Federal pode agir para complicar a vida de políticos, segundo um ministro do STF
item.description: An STF minister claims the Federal Police can undermine political candidacies through selective investigations, leaks, or resource allocation, even without explicit judicial orders. The PF has been accused of prioritizing or abandoning inquiries based on institutional interests, as seen in investigations involving Lulinha, President Lula’s son. The agency is perceived as a destabilizing force in the 2026 elections, capable of influencing outcomes through discreet but impactful actions.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Democracia Cristã registra Clariana Barão para disputar presidência
item.description: The Christian Democracy party has registered Clariana Barão as its presidential candidate for the 2026 elections, running on a pure ticket with Fabiana Torquato as vice-presidential candidate. Barão declared assets worth R$1.82 million to the Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

item.title: Eleições 2026: PCO registra Rui Costa Pimenta ao Planalto com plano de cancelar privatizações
item.description: The Workers' Cause Party (PCO) registered Rui Costa Pimenta as its presidential candidate for the 2026 elections, with Antônio Carlos as his running mate. This marks Pimenta's fourth attempt to reach the presidency. In his electoral registration, he declared no assets to disclose and announced his government plan includes canceling privatizations.

item.title: Davi destrava MP das blusinhas, mas Lula ainda não tem acordo para enterrar taxa
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre secured a pre-agreement to advance the MP that zeroes the 'blusinhas' tax, but no consensus exists on the final text or voting commitment. The MP expires on September 8, and the core dispute centers on whether to maintain the 20% tax on international purchases under US$50, pushed by industry and retail groups, while the government aims to prevent the tax’s return before the elections. The mixed committee meets on September 1, and the rapporteur role is expected to go to the MDB.

item.title: O tamanho do público que campanhas de Lula e Flávio miram nos primeiros atos da campanha
item.description: Lula kicks off his reelection campaign at the Municipal Stadium 1º de Maio in São Bernardo do Campo, expecting 20,000 attendees despite the venue's capacity being limited to 12,578 on match days, in a symbolic event tied to the ABC strikes. Flávio Bolsonaro launches his campaign with an electric truck on Copacabana Beach, without an official crowd estimate, but aiming to match the 64,600-person peak from his father's rally on September 7, 2022.

item.title: STF suspende condenação de Romero Jucá e ex-senador pode concorrer às eleições
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino suspended the conviction of former Senator Romero Jucá for passive corruption and money laundering, removing his ineligibility and allowing him to run in the 2026 elections as a federal deputy candidate. Jucá, who served three consecutive terms as senator for Roraima, was convicted by the TRF1 in July 2024 for receiving R$150,000 from Odebrecht to benefit his son’s campaign. The STF ruled the case must be judged by the Supreme Court, not the Federal Justice.

item.title: STF suspende condenação de Romero Jucá e ex-senador fica apto a disputar eleição
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino suspended the conviction of former senator Romero Jucá for passive corruption and money laundering, nullifying the ineligibility effects and allowing him to run in the 2026 elections. The ruling was based on the TRF-1’s lack of jurisdiction, with the case to be transferred to the STF. Jucá, a pre-candidate for federal deputy from Roraima, can now register his candidacy before the Saturday deadline.

item.title: TSE deve ter "bom senso" para julgar IA de Bolsonaro, diz ex-ministro
item.description: Former TSE minister Admar Gonzaga states that the court already has sufficient legislation to analyze the use of AI in electoral videos, arguing that common sense should guide case-by-case judgments without needing to change rules for every new technology. He emphasizes that the Electoral Justice must interpret existing norms in light of each situation, particularly regarding the deepfake video of Jair Bolsonaro used at the PL convention.

item.title: Como está a disputa Lula x Flávio, segundo as pesquisas da semana sobre a eleição presidencial
item.description: This week's polls show Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a technical tie in the Quaest and BTG/Nexus surveys, with differences within the margin of error. The CNT/MDA poll gives Lula a wider lead at 48% to 39.1%, though it notes a narrowing of his advantage from previous surveys. In the first round, Lula leads across all polls, with margins ranging from 5 to 13.7 points.

item.title: STF suspende condenação do ex-senador Romero Jucá
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino suspended the conviction of former Senator Romero Jucá (MDB-RR) for passive corruption and money laundering, ordering the case to be reheard by the STF due to lack of jurisdiction by the TRF-1. The ruling also nullifies the ineligibility stemming from the conviction, allowing Jucá to run for office again if he chooses. His defense hailed the decision as a restoration of justice and truth.

item.title: Números da Quaest, por que Lula segue favorito e a questão que conta
item.description: Lula remains the favorite in 2026 election polls despite a recent fluctuation placing him in a technical tie with Flávio Bolsonaro within the margin of error. The author argues that structural fundamentals — social programs, economic gains, and sovereignty defense — favor the petista, while the Bolsonarist campaign relies on apocalyptic rhetoric and attacks on the STF, which the author deems fraudulent. Although uncertainty has grown due to social media, the trend still points to a Lula victory, though not by a landslide.

item.title: Clariana Barão declara R$ 1,8 milhão em bens ao TSE; Fabiana Torquato, vice na chapa, informa R$ 2,2 milhões
item.description: Clariana Barão, the Democratic Christian Party's presidential candidate, declared R$1.8 million in assets to the TSE, mainly consisting of real estate and a Land Rover. Her running mate, Fabiana Torquato, reported R$2.2 million in assets, highlighted by a farm in Goiás and an apartment in Brasília. Both are lawyers, and this marks the first time since 1995 that the DC's presidential nominee is not its founder, José Maria Eymael.

item.title: Prazo para pedir voto em trânsito vai até 20 de agosto
item.description: The deadline to request absentee voting (voto em trânsito) for the October 2026 elections is August 20, available online via the TSE website or in person at electoral offices. This allows voters to cast ballots outside their home municipality, subject to rules based on state and city, with no changes permitted after the deadline.

item.title: Ex-ministro da Saúde de Bolsonaro afasta ‘comoção’ sobre Fauci: ‘Flávio se vacinou’
item.description: Former Health Minister Marcelo Queiroga, PL candidate for Senate in Paraíba, defends his COVID-19 vaccination record and criticizes the Lula government for delays in drug incorporation into the public health system, while distancing himself from the controversy surrounding Anthony Fauci’s U.S. Senate hearing, which sparked anti-vaccine attacks by Bolsonaro allies like Nikolas Ferreira and Eduardo Bolsonaro.

item.title: Com envelhecimento da população, eleitorado jovem recua 22% em 16 anos
item.description: The Brazilian electorate aged 16 to 24 decreased by 22% in relative terms and 5.5 million in absolute numbers from 2010 to 2026, dropping from 24.7 million to 19.2 million voters. Despite a 17% increase in the total electorate (from 135.8 million to 158.8 million), youth participation fell from 18.2% to 12.5%, while voters aged 60+ grew by 74%, exceeding 36.8 million. This demographic shift reduces the political weight of youth, though they remain strategically important in close elections.

item.title: Eleitorado jovem no Brasil diminui 22% e muda perfil das urnas
item.description: The Brazilian electorate aged 16 to 24 declined by 22% from 2010 to 2026, dropping from 24.7 million to 19.2 million voters, with their share falling from 18.2% to 12.5%. This aging trend is amplified by a 74% increase in voters over 60, now totaling 36.8 million. The shift reshapes electoral geography, especially in the South and Southeast, and demands adaptive campaign strategies amid intense political polarization.

item.title: O impacto da prisão de Jair Bolsonaro na campanha de Michelle
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro, Senate candidate for the Federal District, says she will not have time to fulfill many electoral commitments due to Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest and decisions by Minister Alexandre de Moraes that limit her support network. She plans to campaign mainly through social media videos, framing the situation as an unjust impediment by the STF preventing her from meeting voters, despite her potential to play a more active role in the Bolsonarist campaign.

item.title: Por que debates em São Paulo têm clima de 2° turno antecipado
item.description: The first São Paulo gubernatorial debate, hosted by Band, featured only Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT), excluding four other candidates due to electoral law requiring parties to have at least five congressional representatives. The absence of candidates from smaller parties (PCB, PCO, PSTU, UP) sparked criticism, with Mandi Coelho (PSTU) filing a formal complaint for inclusion, which the network rejected citing 'editorial relevance'.

item.title: Caiado declara mais que o dobro do patrimônio de 2022
item.description: Presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) declared R$ 52,56 million in assets, 111% more than the R$ 24,87 million he reported in 2022 when running for re-election as governor of Goiás. His team attributes the increase mainly to the sale of Fazenda Santa Maria. The declaration was made in the context of his 2026 presidential bid.

item.title: Campanha de Lula evita 'cascas de banana', mas ajustes econômicos devem vir já em 2026
item.description: Lula's re-election campaign aims to avoid negative surprises by announcing fiscal adjustment projects in advance, but signals that structural proposals may only be sent in 2026 if he wins the election. The campaign's economic coordination prioritizes stability and predictability in economic measures, avoiding 'banana peels' that could trigger market volatility.

item.title: O dia seguinte (por André Gustavo Stumpf)
item.description: The 2026 election campaign overlooks Brazil’s severe economic challenges, including debt exceeding R$10 trillion, sub-2% growth, and costly fuel subsidies that strain public finances. Despite looming post-election inflation from subsidy removals, candidates avoid substantive economic proposals, favoring peripheral issues. Victory will go to the least rejected candidate, not the one with the best plan, revealing a culture that prioritizes symbolism over substance.

item.title: Horário eleitoral não é gratuito e custa milhões em renúncia fiscal
item.description: The mandatory electoral broadcast time is not free, as its cost is covered by tax renunciations granted to radio and TV broadcasters in exchange for airing political propaganda. In the 2022 elections, this amounted to R$737 million in tax exemptions, and between 2014 and 2025, the total reached R$5.2 billion. Airtime is distributed unevenly: 10% equally among parties and 90% proportional to the size of each party's caucus in the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: Pode investigar. É seu direito. Está na Constituição
item.description: The text critiques the selective application of Brazil's constitutional protection of journalistic source secrecy, arguing that authorities invoke it as a 'shield' to justify rights restrictions when it serves power, but disregard it when it threatens allies or targets opponents. It denounces the hypocrisy of upholding the Constitution only when convenient to the establishment, while silencing journalists, lawmakers, and citizens under pretexts of security or order. The case of journalist Luiz Pablo in Maranhão is framed as another instance of this power logic that erodes rights to protect elites and criminalizes dissent.

item.title: Flávio lidera interações nas redes sobre segurança, e Caiado, número de posts
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) led engagement intentions on public security in digital debates among 2026 presidential candidates, while former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) recorded the highest number of posts on the topic.

item.title: Campanha ganha cara de MMA
item.description: The latest Quaest poll shows Lula's lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff has narrowed to just three points, indicating a technical tie. With 50 days until the election, the political climate is heating up, forecasting a period of intense polarization and possible confrontations. The campaign is taking on an aggressive tone, resembling an MMA fight.
